queue: ts (task-spooler) on gpu 0, one job per kernel family

constraints_honoured.preflight_bypass_reason: preflight_check executes on the real GPU (PI ruling 6.1.1); the anchor exists to be diffed against a later run and must not carry an unaccounted extra execution. Stated at the top of every output_<family>.log
constraints_honoured.nvidia_smi_usage: read-only --query-gpu telemetry before and after each family
constraints_honoured.invocations: 3 independent PROCESSES per config, 100 trials each

why_three_rounds: v1: the elementwise kernels used one-element-per-thread indexing, so the deliberately-poor '1 block' config silently computed only 1024 elements and reported ~0.4 us. A broken measurement wearing a terrible config's clothes; an anchor set containing one is worse than none. Fixed with grid-stride loops.
v2: k_block_sum's shared tile was REDUCE_TILE=256 while the sweep also ran block=1024 configs -- an out-of-bounds shared-memory write. Fixed to 1024.

v2 also exposed the worst of the three: the block size was passed as dim3.z while the kernels index with threadIdx.x, so EVERY 1-D config ran with one active thread per block. v3 fixes the block tuple to (block, 1, 1) and re-measures everything.

post_processing.note: CPU-only merge of the four family files into metrics.json. Re-run after the review fixes: the ms/s unit error (bytes/ms is 1000x short of bytes/s) and the memory ceiling (now taken from the HBM-bound n=2^26 cell at 1541 GB/s instead of the L2-resident n=2^22 cell at ~3.2 TB/s). No re-measurement: the underlying ts jobs are unchanged and still authoritative.

note: All 13 jobs are finished; nothing is left running. The superseded v1/v2 logs are kept deliberately: a reader diffing v1 against v3 can see exactly which of my own defects moved the numbers, which is the same evidence standard the lab holds the rest of the epic to.
